(Trenton, New Jersey) | college = * [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] (2020–2023) * [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 43 | draft_team = [[Utah Jazz]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team2 = →[[Capital City Go-Go]] | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] ([[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) }} '''Jamir Kamal Watkins''' (born July 6, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. ==Early life== Raised in [[Trenton, New Jersey]], Watkins attended [[Trenton Catholic Academy]] in [[Mercer County, New Jersey]]. Coming out of high school, Watkins was rated as a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]].{{cite web |last=Epps |first=Wayne |title=VCU adds third player in 2020 recruiting class, with commitment of small forward Jamir Watkins |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/plus/vcu-adds-third-player-in-2020-recruiting-class-with-commitment-of-small-forward-jamir-watkins/article_912df4a0-d621-11e9-867d-8b8f0799af70.html |website=Richmond Times-Dispatch |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=September 13, 2019}} ==College career== ===VCU=== As a freshman in 2020–21, Watkins appeared in 26 games with two starts, where he averaged 7.2 points, 2.6 rebounds, 0.7 assists and 0.9 steals per game.{{cite web |title=Jamir Watkins 2020-21 Game Logs |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jamir-watkins-1/gamelog/2021 |website=Sports Reference |access-date=March 1, 2025}} He missed the entire 2021–22 season due to a knee injury.{{cite web |last=Schultz |first=Nick |title=Report: Florida State transfer guard Jamir Watkins to visit St. John's, Michigan |url=https://www.on3.com/news/jamir-watkins-florida-state-transfer-guard-visit-st-johns-michigan-portal/ |website=On3.com |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=June 4, 2024}} On December 17, 2022, Watkins scored 22 points versus the [[2022–23 Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball team|Northern Illinois]].{{cite web |last=Pearrell |first=Tim |title=VCU sophomore Jamir Watkins starting to show ‘high ceiling’ |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/schools/virginia-commonwealth-university/vcu-sophomore-jamir-watkins-starting-to-show-high-ceiling/article_d0fcfa32-b6e1-11ed-9a51-a7b5e5b60957.html |website=Richmond Times-Dispatch |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=February 27, 2023}} On January 20, 2023, he scored a game-high 15 points, while also adding ten rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks, in a win over [[2022–23 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]].{{cite web |last=Teel |first=David |title=Teel: Jamir Watkins' best game as a collegian ignites VCU's win at Richmond |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/schools/virginia-commonwealth-university/teel-jamir-watkins-best-game-as-a-collegian-ignites-vcus-win-at-richmond/article_48957bcc-993d-11ed-8be7-cbdd4375ae06.html |website=Richmond Times-Dispatch |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=January 21, 2023}} In the first round of the A-10 conference tournament, Watkins scored 11 points, while also tallying six rebounds, two assists and three blocks.{{cite web |last=Pearrell |first=Tim |title=Jamir Watkins seems to be elevating more for VCU as Rams head into A-10 semifinals |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/schools/virginia-commonwealth-university/jamir-watkins-seems-to-be-elevating-more-for-vcu-as-rams-head-into-a-10/article_bfe10662-bef7-11ed-8c46-d7f8a1bf9dcc.html |website=Richmond Times-Dispatch |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=March 10, 2023}} In the 2022–23 season, he averaged 9.5 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web |last=Kassim |first=Ehsan |title=Florida State men's basketball adds VCU SF from transfer portal, second addition |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2023/04/15/fsu-mens-basketball-vcu-sf-jamir-watkins-commits-to-seminoles/70118847007/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=April 15, 2023}} After the season, Watkins entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web |last=Barber |first=Mike |title=VCU transfer Jamir Watkins leads Florida State into Virginia game |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/vcu-transfer-jamir-watkins-leads-florida-state-into-virginia-game/article_6bf8c302-c700-11ee-b26d-33459bb9b9fe.html |website=Richmond Times-Dispatch |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=February 9, 2024}} ===Florida State=== Watkins transferred to play for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. On January 23, 2024, he notched 27 points and 11 rebounds in a win over [[2023–24 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]].{{cite web |last=Kassim |first=Ehsan |title=FSU men's basketball continues hot run with dominant second half win over Syracuse |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2024/01/23/jamir-watkins-career-night-leads-fsu-to-major-road-victory-over-syracuse/72331182007/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=January 23, 2024}} In the second round of the 2024 ACC tournament, Watkins scored a career-high 34 points with 11 rebounds and four steals.{{cite web |last=Schultz |first=Nick |title=Jamir Watkins announces plans to withdraw from NCAA transfer portal, return to Florida State |url=https://www.on3.com/college/florida-state-seminoles/news/jamir-watkins-withdraw-ncaa-transfer-portal-return-florida-state/ |website=On3.com |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=June 7, 2024}} During the 2023–24 season, he started all 33 games for Florida State, where he averaged 15.6 points a game, six rebounds and 2.8 assists, while also adding 64 steals and 26 blocks, en route to being named an all-ACC honorable mention. After the season, Watkins declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]], but eventually withdrew and returned to Florida State.{{cite web |last=Rooney |first=Liam |title=FSU basketball's Jamir Watkins had many options in offseason. Here's why he came back |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/2024/10/18/fsu-basketballs-jamir-watkins-leadership-role-leonard-hamilton/75592728007/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=October 18, 2024}} On November 9, 2024, Watkins scored 30 points, while also adding six rebounds and an assist in a win over [[2024–25 Rice Owls men's basketball team|Rice]].{{cite web |last=Rooney |first=Liam |title=FSU men's basketball's Jamir Watkins scores 30 points in 73-65 road win over Rice |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2024/11/10/fsu-mens-basketball-moves-to-2-0-after-30-points-from-jamir-watkins/76171090007/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |access-date=March 1, 2025|date=November 10, 2024}} On December 14, 2024, he dropped 29 points, four rebounds, five assists, a steal and a block in a win over [[2024–25 Tulane Green Wave men's basketball team|Tulane]].{{cite web |last=Derryberry |first=Jace |title=NBA Draft: Florida State's Jamir Watkins Continues to Build on Plug-and-Play Potential |url=https://www.yardbarker.com/college_basketball/articles/nba_draft_florida_states_jamir_watkins_continues_to_build_on_plug_and_play_potential/s1_17089_41418155 |website=yardbarker.com |access-date=March 17, 2026|date=December 16, 2024}} ==Professional career== Watkins was drafted by the [[Washington Wizards]] via the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]] with the 43rd overall pick.{{cite news |last=Holland |first=Peter |title=How FSU star Jamir Watkins can help Washington Wizards after 2025 NBA Draft selection |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2025/06/27/florida-state-jamir-watkins-nba-draft-washington-wizards/84380136007/ |access-date=June 30, 2025 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=June 27, 2025}} He was subsequently signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the team. On February 26, 2026, the Wizards signed Watkins to a two-year, standard NBA contract.{{Cite web|title=Washington Signs Jamir Watkins to NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/washingtonsignsjamir-watkinsto-nba-contract|access-date=March 16, 2026|website=NBA.com|language=en|date=February 26, 2026}} On April 12, Watkins recorded a career-high 24 points during a 130–117 loss to the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web|title=Wizards' Jamir Watkins: Scores career-high 24 points|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-jamir-watkins-scores-career-high-24-points/|access-date=April 25, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He made 50 total appearances (including seven starts) for the Wizards during his rookie campaign, posting averages of 7.4 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. On July 1, 2026, Watkins re–signed with Washington on a two–way contract.{{Cite web|title=Wizards' Jamir Watkins: Signs with Washington|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-jamir-watkins-signs-with-washington/|access-date=August 5, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
